question.worked_solution:
The difference of squares formula is given by

$$
{a}^{2}-{b}^{2}=(a+b)(a-b)
$$

Notice that all of the terms have a common factor of $q.$ To simplify the computation, we can factor out the $q,$ as follows:

$$
q-q{p}^{4}=q(1-{p}^{4})
$$

The expression in parenthesis can be written as a difference of squares:

$$
q(1-{p}^{4})=q({1}^{2}-{({p}^{2})}^{2})
$$

Now, we factor our expression using the difference of squares formula:

$$
q({1}^{2}-{({p}^{2})}^{2})=q(1+{p}^{2})(1-{p}^{2})
$$

Finally, we notice that the expression in the second set of parentheses is also a difference of squares. Therefore, the expression can be factored further, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}q(1+{p}^{2})(1-{p}^{2}) & =q(1+{p}^{2})({1}^{2}-{p}^{2}) \\  & =q(1+{p}^{2})(1+p)(1-p)\end{aligned}
$$
